definition: Accolade means high praise, special distinction.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word accolade. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know accolade should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Being asked to carry the guild banner at the harvest parade is the highest accolade the growers can give one of their own.
An honorable mention is the smallest coin of recognition — real, but a long way below an accolade.
An award is solid recognition, yet accolade reaches higher still: it names the crowning distinction a whole field looks up to.

An honor is any mark of respect — an invitation to speak, a seat at the head table, a flag flown for you. An accolade is narrower: praise for merit made official and nameable. Every accolade is an honor, but many honors involve no praise at all.

Distinction is the standing that sets you above your peers, built up over years and carried wherever you go — nobody hands it over in a box. An accolade is the opposite kind of thing: a single conferred token, the medal, the title, the prize presented on a particular day.

Brigid's Hospital confers the Lampline Pin, a small silver badge first struck in 1931.
It goes to one nurse, chosen by the whole floor staff, and the criteria have never changed: skill, calm, and kindness under the worst conditions.
This year the pin went to Amara Osei, and the ward treated the news like a coronation.
Colleagues who had worked beside her for a decade said the accolade was overdue; patients wrote in when the newsletter announced it.
Amara keeps the pin in its box at the nurses' station, she says, 'so the night shift remembers the praise belongs to the floor.'
